text: Energy-minimize a solvated alanine dipeptide (OPC water) before heating it: 2000 cycles, the first 1000 of them steepest descent.

Heat the minimized alanine dipeptide system from 0 K to 300 K at constant volume over 20 ps, starting with no velocities: raise the target temperature linearly over the first 18 ps, then hold it at 300 K for the last 2 ps.
Run 10 ns of NPT production for the alanine dipeptide system at 300 K, continuing from the heating run.

Minimize the water and ions around the solvated RAMP1 extracellular domain while holding the protein (residues 1-81) in place with 100 kcal/mol/A^2 positional restraints: 1000 cycles, the first 20 steepest descent.

Heat the solvated RAMP1 system from 100 K to 298 K over 1 ns at constant volume, starting fresh with velocities drawn at 100 K and raising the target temperature linearly across the whole run, with 100 kcal/mol/A^2 restraints on residues 1-81.
Continue the RAMP1 relaxation for 1 ns at constant pressure and 298 K so the box density can relax, picking up from the heating run, with residues 1-81 still restrained at 100 kcal/mol/A^2.
Next RAMP1 relaxation step: 1 ns at constant pressure and 298 K, continuing from the previous step, with the restraint on residues 1-81 lowered to 10 kcal/mol/A^2.
Minimize the RAMP1 system again, now restraining only the protein backbone atoms (CA, N and C) at 10 kcal/mol/A^2: 1000 cycles, the first 30 steepest descent.

After the backbone-restrained minimization, run 1 ns of constant-pressure MD at 298 K, starting fresh with velocities assigned at 298 K, with the backbone atoms CA, N and C restrained at 10 kcal/mol/A^2.
Continue the RAMP1 relaxation for 1 ns at constant pressure and 298 K from the previous step, with the backbone (CA, N, C) restraints lowered to 1 kcal/mol/A^2.
Run another 1 ns of constant-pressure relaxation of RAMP1 at 298 K, continuing from the previous step, with the backbone (CA, N, C) restraints lowered to 0.1 kcal/mol/A^2.
Final RAMP1 relaxation step: remove all restraints and simulate 1 ns at constant pressure and 298 K, continuing from the previous step.
Run a 50 ns constant-pressure production simulation of the RAMP1 protein in a truncated octahedral box of explicit water at 300 K, continuing from the equilibrated system.
Write the input for a 10 ns constant-pressure MD run of the solvated RAMP1 protein (truncated octahedral box) at 300 K, continuing from the equilibrated system.
Minimize a B-DNA polyA-polyT decamer in vacuum (no periodic box, no implicit solvent) before MD: 500 cycles, the first 250 steepest descent, with a 12 Angstrom nonbonded cutoff.
Run 100 ps of MD on the DNA decamer in vacuum (no periodic box, no implicit solvent) at 300 K with a 12 Angstrom cutoff, assigning initial velocities at 300 K.
Minimize the whole solvated DNA decamer system (TIP3P water, Na+ counterions) with no restraints: 2500 cycles, the first 1000 steepest descent.
The solvated DNA decamer has been heated at constant volume; now switch to constant pressure (1 bar) and run 100 ps of unrestrained MD at 300 K, continuing from the heating run.

Write one 200 ps segment of constant-pressure MD (1 bar, 300 K, no restraints) for a solvated A-DNA polyA-polyT decamer (TIP3P, Na+), continuing from the previous segment; it will be repeated nine times for 1.8 ns in total.
Equilibrate the solvated PPAT-pantetheine protein system for 100 ns at 300 K and 1 bar to adjust the density, continuing from the heating run, with no restraints.
Run 100 ns of production MD for the PPAT-pantetheine system at constant volume and 300 K (NVT), continuing from the NPT equilibration, with no restraints.

Relax a solvated protein (PDB 1RGG, chain A) by energy minimization: 1000 cycles of conjugate gradient, with the backbone atoms CA, N and O of residues 1-96 held by 10 kcal/mol/A^2 positional restraints.

Heat the minimized 1RGG protein system from 150 K to 300 K over 10 ps at constant volume, starting fresh with velocities assigned at 150 K, with 10 kcal/mol/A^2 restraints on the backbone atoms CA, N and O of residues 1-96.
Equilibrate the heated 1RGG system for 5 ps at 300 K and 1 bar, continuing from the heating run, with the backbone CA, N and O atoms of residues 1-96 restrained at 10 kcal/mol/A^2.
Continue equilibrating the 1RGG system without restraints for 1 ns at 300 K and 1 bar, picking up from the previous run.
Run 250 ps of oxytocin production dynamics in explicit water at 300 K and 1 bar, continuing from the equilibration, with no restraints.
Minimize the solvated HIV protease-inhibitor complex (PDB 1HVR) for 1000 cycles of steepest descent, holding the heavy atoms of residues 1-199 with 5 kcal/mol/A^2 restraints.
Run 2 ns of unrestrained constant-pressure production for the solvated 4QMZ protein-ligand complex at 298.15 K, continuing from equilibration.
First preparation step for the solvated 3WZE complex: minimize only the hydrogens by restraining every non-hydrogen atom at 5 kcal/mol/A^2, using 5000 cycles of steepest descent.
Equilibration step 7 for the solvated 1NDV complex: 50 ps of constant-pressure MD at 298.15 K, continuing from step 6, with the heavy atoms of residues 1-350 restrained at 0.5 kcal/mol/A^2.

Minimize the solvated 1G2L protein-ligand complex with the heavy atoms of residues 1-292 restrained at 5 kcal/mol/A^2, so mainly hydrogens, water and ions relax: 5000 cycles, the first 2500 steepest descent.

Run a short 50 ps MD stage that heats and equilibrates the minimized 1G2L complex at constant pressure toward 298.15 K, starting from the minimized coordinates without velocities, with the heavy atoms of residues 1-292 restrained at 5 kcal/mol/A^2.
Equilibrate the 1G2L complex for 100 ps at 298.15 K and 1 bar, starting fresh from coordinates only, with weak 1 kcal/mol/A^2 restraints on the heavy atoms of residues 1-292.

Equilibrate the 1G2L complex for 50 ps at constant pressure and 298.15 K, continuing from the previous step, restraining only the protein backbone atoms CA, C and N of residues 1-291 at 0.1 kcal/mol/A^2 so the ligand moves freely.

Run 10 ns of constant-pressure production MD for the 1G2L complex at 298.15 K, continuing from the last equilibration, with weak 0.1 kcal/mol/A^2 restraints on the backbone atoms CA, C and N of residues 1-291.

Minimize the solvent around the solvated MTR1 ribozyme: 500 cycles of conjugate gradient, restraining the solute heavy atoms (every non-hydrogen atom except the NA, CL and MG ions and WAT water) at 50 kcal/mol/A^2.

Heat the solvated MTR1 ribozyme at constant volume from 0 K (no initial velocities) to 300 K over a 1.6 ns run, restraining the solute heavy atoms (every non-hydrogen atom except the NA, CL and MG ions and WAT water) at 50 kcal/mol/A^2.

Equilibrate the solvent around the MTR1 ribozyme for 5 ns at 300 K and 1 bar, continuing from the heating run, with the solute heavy atoms (every non-hydrogen atom except the NA, CL and MG ions and WAT water) restrained at 50 kcal/mol/A^2.
Minimize the whole solvated MTR1 ribozyme system with the positional restraints released, so solute and solvent relax against each other: 500 cycles of conjugate gradient.

Reheat the MTR1 ribozyme system at constant volume from 0 K (no initial velocities) to 300 K over a 1.6 ns run, with the solute heavy atoms (every non-hydrogen atom except the NA, CL and MG ions and WAT water) restrained at 25 kcal/mol/A^2.

Equilibrate the MTR1 ribozyme for 500 ps at 300 K and 1 bar, continuing from the previous stage, with the solute heavy atoms (every non-hydrogen atom except the NA, CL and MG ions and WAT water) restrained at 25 kcal/mol/A^2.

Next MTR1 equilibration stage: lower the restraints on the solute heavy atoms (every non-hydrogen atom except the NA, CL and MG ions and WAT water) to 10 kcal/mol/A^2 and run 500 ps at 300 K and 1 bar, continuing from the previous stage.
Continue the MTR1 equilibration for 500 ps at 300 K and 1 bar, with the solute heavy atoms (every non-hydrogen atom except the NA, CL and MG ions and WAT water) now restrained at 5 kcal/mol/A^2.

Final MTR1 equilibration before production: 500 ps at 300 K and 1 bar, continuing from the previous stage, with weak 2 kcal/mol/A^2 restraints on the solute heavy atoms (every non-hydrogen atom except the NA, CL and MG ions and WAT water).
